upstream:          https://github.com/y-256/libdivsufsort
tag:               2.0.1
head_sha:          82b01f764e342f1858d4473c17b56844aac9c12d
license:           MIT (expat-form; see COPYING)
spdx-id:           MIT
canonical citation: Yuta Mori, "libdivsufsort: A lightweight suffix sorting library", 2003-2008.

scope vendored:
  full tree at tag 2.0.1, minus .git/.

build configuration (CMake shim at third_party/libdivsufsort/CMakeLists.txt
forces these options on top of upstream's CMakeLists.txt):
  - BUILD_DIVSUFSORT64 = OFF   (32-bit suffix array only; the RLZ reference
                                never exceeds 1 GB on any evaluated column,
                                so 32-bit indices suffice)
  - BUILD_SHARED_LIBS  = OFF
Used by runners/rlz/rlz_core.cpp inside the compress timed region.

Why the RLZ baseline is a reimplementation rather than a vendored upstream:
the canonical academic implementation (skuruppu/RLZ, GPL-3.0, HEAD
0e168d9900ac7d357a44d622834d1cac7d4a1d40) is structurally unsuitable for an
in-process harness:
  (a) no in-process API — RLZCompress() takes argv-style filename arrays and
      reads/writes files on disk inside the constructor;
  (b) output is a custom on-disk binary format, so capturing it would mean
      reparsing its bit-encoder state;
  (c) it requires vendoring libcds 1.0.8 (GPL-3.0-or-later), adding a large
      transitive GPL surface.
The harness therefore ships a compact C++ implementation of the
Hoobin/Puglisi/Zobel (VLDB 2011) algorithm — greedy LZ77 factor parse
against a uniformly sampled reference, suffix-array longest-match lookup —
in runners/rlz/rlz_core.{h,cpp} (~200 lines), with libdivsufsort 2.0.1 as
its sole external dependency. The reference is sampled with a fixed seed
(std::mt19937, seed=42), matching the published method. Rationale and
configuration details: docs/benchmark/fairness/rlz.md.
